raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Settle in.","source_id":"GLUE_PACING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"You're starting in the Île de la Cité.","source_id":"SYNTHESIZED_OPENER","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"When you're ready, head for Pont Neuf — it's just ahead.","source_id":"SYNTHESIZED_OPENER","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Picture a king taking a running leap over a half-built arch, and his workmen roaring with delight.","source_id":"1fbeb1b3-ce04-44eb-ad7c-dcd624059a0a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"That was Henri IV, one of the city's first great town-planners, who built this bridge and kept coming back to watch it rise.","source_id":"1fbeb1b3-ce04-44eb-ad7c-dcd624059a0a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Its name means New Bridge — and yet it's the oldest bridge still standing in Paris.","source_id":"1fbeb1b3-ce04-44eb-ad7c-dcd624059a0a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0,"also_cites":["4cb9c5a0-f2ec-47ea-8afb-ae44d53fe06a"]},{"text":"So why \"new\"? Because it broke every rule of its day: twelve arches of solid stone, and not one house crowding the roadway.","source_id":"1fbeb1b3-ce04-44eb-ad7c-dcd624059a0a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0,"also_cites":["4cb9c5a0-f2ec-47ea-8afb-ae44d53fe06a"]},{"text":"Those semicircular bays along the sides once held market stalls — teeth-pullers, quack doctors, and hawkers of every kind.","source_id":"4cb9c5a0-f2ec-47ea-8afb-ae44d53fe06a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Look to the middle of the span — that bronze horseman is Henri IV, and he's keeping a secret.","source_id":"GLUE_STAGING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The first statue rose in 1614, and revolutionaries tore it down in 1792.","source_id":"968b7287-51a9-4e51-924b-5a9f57cebdbe","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"When the Bourbons returned, Parisians paid to rebuild it in 1818 by public subscription.","source_id":"968b7287-51a9-4e51-924b-5a9f57cebdbe","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The bronze came from melting down a statue of the general Louis Charles Antoine Desaix, and the new figure was cast from a mould that had survived from the original.","source_id":"968b7287-51a9-4e51-924b-5a9f57cebdbe","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Before the sculptor François-Frédéric Lemot sealed it up, he tucked four boxes inside — a life of Henri IV, a 17th-century parchment certifying the first statue, a note on how this one was commissioned, and the names of everyone who'd contributed.","source_id":"968b7287-51a9-4e51-924b-5a9f57cebdbe","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Just off the bridge, at the Place Dauphine, one day a year turned into a lottery for young artists.","source_id":"70806017-6a80-4dde-be41-aa0d0ce7928a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"On the Petite Fête-Dieu — the \"Small Corpus Christi,\" eight days after the main feast — painters hung their canvases outdoors, but only from six in the morning until noon.","source_id":"70806017-6a80-4dde-be41-aa0d0ce7928a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"It was an unofficial salon, a rare chance for an unknown to be noticed, and a forerunner of the Salon des Refusés that would later spark the Impressionists.","source_id":"70806017-6a80-4dde-be41-aa0d0ce7928a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"In 1720, a twenty-two-year-old — the son of the man who kept the king's billiards — set out an antique bas-relief here.","source_id":"70806017-6a80-4dde-be41-aa0d0ce7928a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The painter J.-B. Vanloo stopped, studied it a long while, found real quality, bought it, and took the young man under his wing.","source_id":"70806017-6a80-4dde-be41-aa0d0ce7928a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Eight years on, that unknown was Vanloo's colleague at the Academy of Painting. His name was Jean-Baptiste-Siméon Chardin.","source_id":"70806017-6a80-4dde-be41-aa0d0ce7928a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"As you cross, look along the parapet: 381 carved stone faces, and no two alike.","source_id":"87c8ae7c-7a79-4c4c-a890-6e1fd56e204f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"They're woodland gods, satyrs and sylvains out of old mythology, copied from originals by the Renaissance sculptor Germain Pilon — the man who carved the tomb of Henri II and Catherine de' Medici at Saint-Denis.","source_id":"87c8ae7c-7a79-4c4c-a890-6e1fd56e204f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Pilon's originals lasted until the bridge was rebuilt between 1851 and 1854.","source_id":"87c8ae7c-7a79-4c4c-a890-6e1fd56e204f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Six went to the Musée Carnavalet and eight to the Cluny, and today they all sit at the Musée National de la Renaissance at the Château d'Écouen.","source_id":"87c8ae7c-7a79-4c4c-a890-6e1fd56e204f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The new copies came from Maindron, Lavigne, Barye and Fontenelle — Fontenelle alone cut 61, on the upstream side between the right bank and the island.","source_id":"87c8ae7c-7a79-4c4c-a890-6e1fd56e204f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Now here's something you'll have to imagine, because it happened right where you're standing.","source_id":"6f0823bb-f457-4925-b0fa-ba9c588b68cd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"You've likely heard that Louis Daguerre's 1838 view of the Boulevard du Temple is the first photograph to show a human being.","source_id":"6f0823bb-f457-4925-b0fa-ba9c588b68cd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"But two years earlier, in 1836 or 1837, Daguerre was testing his new technique outdoors, and one of those tests pointed straight at the Pont Neuf and its statue of Henri IV.","source_id":"6f0823bb-f457-4925-b0fa-ba9c588b68cd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Down in the lower-left, in the statue's shadow, you can make out what looks like a worker, maybe two, lying against the fence.","source_id":"6f0823bb-f457-4925-b0fa-ba9c588b68cd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"If the dating holds, that faint shape — not the man on the Boulevard du Temple — may be the first human ever photographed.","source_id":"6f0823bb-f457-4925-b0fa-ba9c588b68cd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"And those steps beside the statue lead down to the square du Vert-Galant, where Jacques de Molay, Grand Master of the Templars, was burned at the stake — cursing the kings of France as the flames took him.","source_id":"1cc3a923-e93c-490f-9dc5-55cb6a79c465","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0}]}
